Number of studies.evidence_source: Section presents regression analyses separated by sex ("In women, the first step..." and "In men, the first step..."), indicating analyses from a single study reported separately for women and men.

section_summary.extract_value: This section reports regression analyses predicting erotophilia separately for women and men. For women, the second step of the regression was significant with body appreciation and sexual orientation significant predictors; for men, only the second step was significant and body appreciation was the sole significant predictor.
section_summary.evidence_source: "In women, the first step of the regression with erotophilia was significant, F(4, 146) = 4.03, p = .004, Adj. R^2 = .08, with only sexual orientation emerging as a significant predictor (...) The second step of the regression was also significant, F(8, 142) = 4.93, p < .001, ΔR^2 = .10, with body appreciation (B = .30, SE = .09, β = .38, t = 3.13, p = .002) and sexual orientation (...)" and "In men, the first step of the regression was not significant, F(4, 158) < 1, Adj. R^2 < .01, whereas the second step was significant, F(8, 154) = 2.24, p = .027, ΔR^2 = .06, with body appreciation emerging as the only significant predictor (B = .18, SE = .06, β = .32, t = 2.95, p = .004)."
